tei:div.tei:note: The lesson reports for Gerhard Alberesheim in the original are written continuously, without paragraph breaks or separating punctuation. They have been separated here in the interests of legibility.
tei:div.tei:ab: 5. X. Chopin Etude Am op. 25 No 11.Albersheim attended on September 25 for “first introduction to the plan of tuition provided.”
8. Kontrapunkt, zweist. Satz, 1. Gattung begonnen.
11. Mozart Klavier-Sonate Adur (wegen Vortrag).
25. Aufriß der Etude.
29. Zum Vortrag der hohen Messe.
5. XI. Dreist. Satz.

29. Ueber Handschriften im Allgemeinen u. im Besonderen über eine Stelle in der IV. Sinf. v. Beethoven: his–cis oder h–cis (1. Satz).Schenker is referring to the lower neighbor-note figure in the first violins at bar 290, toward the end of the development. The autograph score reads: d2–c2–b1–c2. So does Simrock’s 1823 edition of the score. But the old Gesamtausgabe and the Eulenburg score (edited by Max Unger) both give b1. Modern editions of the symphony, however, restore the autograph reading.
3. XII. Aufklärung der Stelle in Beethoven durch Parallelismus, s. Freier Satz; einiges aus dem Forellenquintett.
13. Allerlei aus Mozart Sonaten.
17. Ueber den Unterschied von Rosé u. v. Berg.

20. Ueber eine Stelle in Wagners „Tristan“, Bülow Klavierauszug S. 150 u. 165;In Hans von Bülow’s vocal score of the opera, p. 150 marks the introduction of the “Liebestod” music (Tristan: “So starben wir, um ungetrennt”) in the Act II love duet; an orchestral variation of this theme appears on p. 165. zum Philharmonischen Konzert am 29., zur Egmont Ouvertüre, V. Sinf. u. op. 106.The diary for December 19 has a lengthy description of this concert, which begins: “At the Philharmonic concert: “Egmont” Overture: all upbeats comprising three eighth notes not played as upbeats – without striving toward a goal tone. As a result, the overture lost all its life, all its fire. Opus 106: in itself an inexcusable error, which demonstrates that Weingartner is not aware of the difference between a piano and an orchestra, nor of the difference between writing for piano and for orchestra. [...]”
31. Leonoren Ouvertüre 3, besonders die Stelle in As u. 2. Gedanke.

3. I. Aus der Zauberflöte die Arie der Königin der Nacht; die Koloratur restlos in die Stimmführung eingebaut;Cf. Elias’s lesson for January 4: “I show her the Queen of the Night’s aria from The Magic Flute.” Linie des Menuetts.
7. Brahms Studien gezeigt Bl. 1–11.

10. Brahms–Scarlatti gezeigt.This may refer to a part of Brahms’s manuscript collection of keyboard sonatas by Domenico Scarlatti, or more specifically to his copy of the first edition of the Essercizi per gravicembalo, probably acquired in 1856. See Elizabeth McKay, Brahms and Scarlatti, Musical Times, cxxx/10 (October 1989), 586–88.
14. Fragen zu Haydns Streichquartetten.
17. Aus Mendelssohns Schottischer Sinfonie; Brahms II. Sinfonie.
21. Zu Brahms II. Sinf.; eine Arie aus Mozart; vierst. Satz begonnen.
31. Ausblick auf alla Turca. – Fehlt.Diary Jan 31: “Albersheim is taking a holiday, pays his fees for February,” hence the gap between January 31 and February 18. –
18. II. Bruckner VII. Sinf., 1. Satz vierhändig.

21. Einige Fragen für die Schwester aus Mozart Adagio der Variationen. – Fragen aus Haydns Quinten-Quartett Dm, aus Mozarts letztem Streichquartett
Fdur; Bogen aus den Korrekturen, Schönberg betreffend, gezeigt.
28. Aus Tristan: large gap aus dem II. Jhrb.: über das Organische der Sonatenform; den Unterschied in der Auskomponierung überhaupt erläutert.
7. III. Die Mozart-Sonate ganz durchgespielt.
11. Ueber Verdi–Werfel;Franz Werfel’s Verdi: Roman der Oper [Verdi: A Novel of the Opera] was published in 1924. aus der VIII. Sinf. v. Beethoven, 2. u. 3. Satz vierhändig mit Vortragsanweisungen.

18.Diary Feb 10: “From Albersheim (postcard from Switzerland): he will appear on Friday the 18th.” Aus Haydns Streichquartett BdurProbably Op. 76, No. 4 (“Sunrise”), which begins with a series of phrases of irregular length. Fragen der Metrik; Chopin Etude op. 10 No 1: Bass im Mittelteil? Haydn Sinf. Cdur, Adagio,Probably the slow introduction to the first movement of Symphony No. 97, the melodic line of which is highly decorated. freier Vortrag der Diminutionen.
24. Stellen aus Lohengrin.
28.. Chopin-Etude abgeschlossen.
1. IV. Fragen aus Mozarts Streichquartett, meist über den Vortrag.Probably K. 590, which was one of the pieces discussed at the lesson on February 21.

4. Fortsetzung der Mozart-Fragen; über das legatissimo durch Liegenlassen.For a full discussion of the technique of Liegenlassen, see Schenker, The Art of Performance, ed. H. Esser, transl. I. S. Scott (New York: Oxford University Press, 2000), chap. 5, pp. 21–30.
8. 5–8 stimm. Satz.

11. Aus Beethovens Cism-Quartett
das Variationen-Thema, Linie u. Tempo; über die Variationen in Mozarts Streichquartett Dm (durch Gegensatz); über die Melancholia Malinconia in Beethovens Streichquartett op. 18 No 6, Linie u. Tempo; – eine Arie von Spohr: warum sie schlechter sei als eine von Mozart oder Beethoven; einiges zu Strauß’ Don Quichote-Partitur; Versuch einer Linie zu Chopin Etude Am op. 10 No 2. – Fehlt seit 22. IV.From this time until the end of the first week of May, Albersheim had a period of (unspecified) illness.
9. V. Ueber Ersuchen spiele ich vor.Diary May 5: “Albersheim (postcard): he will appear, is doing a few exercises, asks me to keep my promise to play to him!”
13. Aus Mozarts Streichquartett Adur Fragen, namentlich über die Chromen; über den Vortrag des Menuetts; von Joachim u. Rosé; Plan der Variationen: Solo, Moll, Dur.
16. Metrik in Brahms’ „Auf dem Kirchhof“.
19. Einiges aus Brahms’ I. Sinf., 1., 2., 4. Satz zum Furtwängler-Konzert.
23. In Mozarts Streichquartett Am Gdur die Stelle: blank space
27. Mischungsaufgaben.
30. Spiele ihm aus op. 31 No 1 das Adagio vor.

3. VI. Aus Mozarts Streichquartett Ddur No 7:Probably K. 499, which is the seventh of Mozart’s later string quartets and is sometimes so numbered. Fragen über Metrik u. Form, 2. Ged.; aus dem Adagio über scheinbare Synkopen; aus dem letzten Satz Nebennotenfragen.
16. Zwei Ersatzstunden: Kontrapunkt abgeschlossen.Diary June 16: “Albersheim from 10 to 12, an additional lesson (in spite of the holiday).”

17. Fragen aus Mozarts Streichquintett Cdur, aus Mozarts Klaviersonaten; die Urlinie des Ddur-Themas aus der Ddur-Sonate;Cf. Brünauer’s lesson for June 17: “On the variations theme in Mozart’s Sonata in D major.” über Ornamente u. deren Vortrag.
20. . 3–4⁀4–3 mit Beispielen aus Brahms’ Rhapsodie Hm u. Polonaise Cism von Chopin belegt.

tei:div.tei:note: The lesson reports for Gerhard Albersheim in the original are written continuously, without paragraph breaks or separating punctuation. They have been separated here in the interests of legibility.
tei:div.tei:ab: October 5: Chopin Etude in A minor, Op. 25, No. 11.
October 8: Counterpoint in two voices, first species, begun.
October 11: Mozart Piano Sonata in A major (on account of performance).
October 25: Outline of the Etude.
October 29: On the performance of the Mass in B minor.
November 5: Three-part counterpoint.
November 29: On manuscripts in general, and in particular in a passage from Beethoven’s Fourth Symphony: B–C or B–C (in the first movement).
December 3: Explanation of the Beethoven passage by parallelism; see Free Composition; some things from the “Trout” Quintet.
December 13: various things from sonatas by Mozart.
December 17: On the difference between Rosé and van den Berg.
December 20: . On a passage from Wagner’s Tristan, pages 150 and 165 of Bülow's piano-vocal score; for the Philharmonic concert on the 29th, on the "Egmont" Overture, the Fifth Symphony and Op. 106.

December 27: Mozart:
the first movement played for the first time; the Minuet taken up.
December 31: “Leonora” Overture No. 3, especially the passage in A and the second theme.
January 3: The Queen of the Night’s aria from The Magic Flute; the coloratura completely underpinned by the voice-leading; the voice-leading line of the Minuet.
January 7: I show him Brahms’s study, leaves 1–11.
January 10: I show him Brahms–Scarlatti.
January 14: Questions about Haydn’s string quartets.
January 17: Extracts from Mendelssohn’s “Scottish” Symphony and Brahms’s Second Symphony.
January 21: n Brahms’s Second Symphony; an aria by Mozart; four-part counterpoint begun.
January 24: Minuet played; the Urlinie of the trio section studied carefully.
January 31: Glimpse of the Rondo alla turca. – He does not turn up.
February 18: Bruckner’s Seventh Symphony, first movement, played four-hands.

February 21: Some questions for his sister about the Adagio variation in the Mozart. – Questions about Haydn’s “Fifths” Quartet in D minor and Mozart’s last string quartet,
in F major; gatherings from the proofs of the second Meisterwerk yearbook shown, those concerning Schoenberg.
February 28: From Tristan: large gap; from the second Meisterwerk yearbook: On Organicism in Sonata Form; the difference in the composing-out in general explained.
March 7: The Mozart sonata played from beginning to end.
March 11: On Verdi by Werfel; the second and third movements of Beethoven’s Eighth Symphony played four-hands, with performance instructions.

March 18: In Haydn’s String Quartet in B major, questions of metrical organisation; Chopin Etude Op. 10, No. 1: the bass in the middle section? Haydn’s Symphony in C major, Adagio, free interpretation of the diminutions.
March 24: Passages from Lohengrin.
March 28: The Chopin etude completed.
April 1: Questions about Mozart’s string quartet, mainly about performance.
April 4: Continuation of the Mozart questions; on playing legatissimo by holding notes down.
April 8: Counterpoint for five to eight voices.

April 11: From Beethoven’s C minor Quartet
the variation theme, voice-leading line and tempo; on the variations in Mozart’s String Quartet in D minor (by contrast); on La malinconia in Beethoven’s String Quartet Op. 18, No. 6, voice-leading line and tempo; – an aria by Spohr: why it should be worse than one by Mozart or Beethoven; some things about the score of Strauss’s Don Quixote; Attempt at a voice-leading line for Chopin’s Etude in A minor, Op. 10, No. 2. – He will be absent from April 22.
May 9: By request, I play the piano to him.
May 16: Metrical structure in Brahms’s “Auf dem Kirchhof”.
May 19: Some things about the first, second and fourth movements of Brahms’s First Symphony, for Furtwängler’s concert.
May 23: In Mozarts String Quartet in G major, the following passage: blank space
May 27:Assignments in mixed-species counterpoint.
May 30: I play him the Adagio from Op. 31, No. 1.

June 3: In Mozart’s String Quartet No. 7 in D major, questions about metric structure and form in the second theme; concerning apparent tied notes; questions about neighbor notes in the last movement.
June 16: Two make-up lessons: counterpoint studies completed.

June 17: Questions about Mozart’s String Quintet in C major, concerning Mozart’s piano sonatas; the Urlinie of the D major theme from the Sonata in D major; concerning ornaments and their performance.
June 20: 3–4⁀4–3, demonstrated with examples from Brahms’s Rhapsody in B minor and Chopin’s Polonaise in C minor.

tei:div.tei:note: The lesson reports for Robert Brünauer in the original are written continuously, without paragraph breaks or separating punctuation. They have been separated here in the interests of legibility.
tei:div.tei:ab: 4. X. Brahms op. 119 No 1 Bild; Urlinie des Paisiello-Themas Beethoven.Schenker’s diary for Sept 28 records his sending out the “lesson table” to Brünauer and Elias.
7. Fingersatz u. Spiel bei Brahms u. Paisiello Thema u. Var. 1.Diary October 7: “Dr. Brünauer asks if he may bring his fee in two halves; would we receive his lady friend?”
25. Die Variationen zuende.Diary Oct 23: “In the evening, I work on Brahms's Op. 119, No. 2, for Brünauer.”

4. XI.
Beethoven: Eroica-Variationen, neu, Bild des Themas.Diary Nov 4: “Brünauer pays half his fee, in notes of different denominations, among them even silver shillings!!”
8. Brahms, op. 119 No 2, Bild begonnen.
25. Eroica-Variationen abgeschlossen.
29. Die Fuge begonnen.
2. XII. Einiges zum Forellen-Quintett.
6. Bild der Fuge.

9. Fingersatz.Diary Dec 9: “Dr. Brünauer speaks about wanting to acquire a Bechstein piano – I get furious, as I relate this acquisition to his lady friend: to pay me the lesson fees in half-installments, and in addition to make such a great expenditure: that is truly shameless!”

13. Nur Bassbrechungen der Fuge vorgeführt.Diary Dec 12: “The fugue from the "Eroica" Variations newly written out, in ink (for Dr. Brünauer)”. — Diary Dec 15: “Dr. Brünauer asked, via his messenger, whether he could come tomorrow at 5:30, or some other time – this petty bourgeois takes no notice of the previous [pupil], and asserts his right that I can give up my time for sake of his laziness – the repulsive instinct of a person who does not have a drop of decency in his blood.”
20. Einiges zu Weingartners Instrumentierung von op. 106.
23. Beethoven abgeschlossen.
27. Falstaff-Variationen, neu (Bilder).
30. Beide Hefte Liebeslieder-WalzerBrahms’s Liebeslieder, Op.52a and Neue Liebeslieder, Op. 65a. gespielt.

3. I. Ueber den Fingersatz einer Stelle in der Esm-Variation.The fourteenth of the “Eroica” Variations is in E minor, so Schenker is probably referring to that, not the fifth variation of WoO73, which is set in B minor.
13. Falstaff-Variationen abgeschlossen.

17. Bericht über das Furtwängler-Konzert.Concert on January 16 in the Great Hall of the Musikverein Building with the Vienna Philharmonic under Wilhelm Furtwängler, the program comprising Mendelssohn’s Third Symphony (“Scottish”) and Brahms’s Second Symphony.
20. Berçeuse wiederholt, neu: Linie.
3. II. Impromptu Asdur, neu, Linie.Diary Feb 3: “Dr. Brünauer pays for the entire month.” — Diary Feb 4: “In the morning, [...] I work on Chopin's Op. 29 (Impromptu), for Dr. Brünauer.”
7. Impromptu zuende.
10. Das Bild aller Variationen der Berçeuse selbst zuhause geschrieben.

17. Wiederholung der Noc-
-turne Fisdur.
21. Impromptu Fisdur, neu.Diary Feb 20: “I work on Chopin's Impromptu in F major (for Brünauer).”
24. Bild-Korrekturen.
28. Fingersatz.
21. III. Wiederholt Brahms Rhapsodie Hmoll (Bilder).

28. Unterbrechung durch Prof. Altmann.Diary March 28: “I work on the Urlinie of Brahms's Rhapsody in B minor (for Brünauer) [...] From 6:45 until 7:30, Director Altmann (I send Dr. Brünauer away).” – Diary May 14: “Brünauer receives the lesson that had been cancelled on account of Prof. Altmann's visit: four-hand music by Schumann (new) and Haydn.”

31. Ueber das Philharmonische Konzert der Beethoven-Feier.A concert in the Theater an der Wien, marking the centennial of Beethoven’s death, took place on March 27 at 11 a.m.: Program: Fifth Symphony, Violin Concerto, Third Piano Concerto, the Vienna Philharmonic conducted by Martin Spörr, with Hugo Gottesmann and Guido Peters as soloists. That evening, Goethe’s Egmont, with all of Beethoven’s incidental music, was staged at the Staatsoper, with the Vienna Philharmonic under Weingartner and the Klärchen songs sung by Lotte Lehmann.
4. IV. Insbesondere die Coda der Rhapsodie Hmoll.
7. Das 1. Thema aus dem Beethoven-Trio op. 97; neu: Nocturne Esdur op. 9.
21. Nocturne zuende.
28. Vierhändig eine Sinfonie von Haydn, Bd. III, die ich mit Vrieslander gespielt habe.
2. V. Vierhändig aus Schumanns Original-Stücken.
7. Haydn Fantasie gelesen u. eine Sinfonie vierhändig gespielt.
12. Einige Bassmodelle; aus der Nocturne Haydn fortgesetzt.
16. Modelle einzelner Stellen aus der Nocturne Fisdur, Esdur u. aus der Rhapsodie Hmoll zur Befestigung.

2. VI. Zu Haydns Fmoll-Andante
selbständig die Linie dargestellt, sehr gut.Diary June 2: “Mrs. Pairamall and Brünauer pay 50 shillings per lesson!!!”

9. Linie zu Mendelssohns Frühlingslied in der Stunde versucht.Diary June 9: “Work on the Urlinie of the Brahms Rhapsody (for Brünauer).” – Diary June 10: “Urlinie to Mendelssohn's ‘Spring Song’ (for Brünauer) and for Chopin's Prelude in D major (for Elias).”
13. Die neuen Händel-Funde aus der „Musik“ gezeigt; das Cmoll-Stück als von Bach befunden; flüchtiges Durchspielen von Mendelssohn Frühlingslied u. Hmoll-Stück.
15. Ueber die Nebennotenbewegung, genaue Bilder, namentlich Beispiele aus der Polonaise Cismoll.Diary June 15: “Brünauer from 5 to 6, a substitute lesson.”
20. Ueber das Variationen-Thema in Mozarts Sonate Ddur (vgl. Albersheim).Albersheim’s lesson for June 17: “the Urlinie of the D major theme from the D major sonata; on ornaments and their execution.”

tei:div.tei:note: The lesson reports for Robert Brünauer in the original are written continuously, without paragraph breaks or separating punctuation. They have been separated here in the interests of legibility.
tei:div.tei:ab: October 7: Fingering and playing for the Brahms, and for the Paisiello theme and first variation.
October 25: The variations finished.

November 4:
Beethoven: “Eroica” Variations, new, graph of the theme.
November 8: Brahms, Op. 119, No. 2, graph begun.
November 25: “Eroica” Variations completed.
November 29: The fugue begun.
December 2: A few things about the “Trout” Quintet.
December 6: Graph of the fugue.
December 9: Fingering of the fugue.
December 13: Only the bass arpeggiations in the fugue presented.
December 20: Some things about Weingartner’s orchestration of Op. 106.
December 23: Beethoven completed.
December 27: “Falstaff” Variations, new (graphs).
December 30: The two volumes of Liebeslieder waltzes played.
January 3:Concerning the fingering of a passage in the E minor variation.
January 13: “Falstaff” Variations completed.
January 17: Report of the Furtwängler concert.
January 20: Berceuse revisited, new: voice-leading line
February 3: Impromptu in A major, new, voice-leading line.
February 7: Impromptu, Op. 29 finished.
February 10: The graph of all the variations of the Berceuse written by himself at home.

February 17: Revisiting of the
Nocturne in F major.
February 21: Impromptu in F major, new.
February 24: Corrections to the graph.
February 28: Fingering.
March 21: Revisiting of Brahms’s Rhapsody in B minor (graphs).
March 28: Interruption by Prof. Altmann.
March 31: About the Philharmonic concert at the Beethoven festival.
April 4: In particular, the coda of the Rhapsody in B minor.
April 7: The first theme from Beethoven’s Trio, Op. 97; new: Nocturne in E major from Op. 9.
April 21.: Nocturne finished.
April 28:A Symphony by Haydn from vol. III, which I played four-hands with Vrieslander.
May 2:Original piano-four-hand music by Schumann.
May 7: Haydn’s Fantasy read, and a symphony played four-hands.
May 12: A few bass models; Haydn continued.
May 16: Models for a few passages from the Nocturnes in F major and E major, and from the Rhapsody in B minor, for consolidation.

June 2: The voice-leading line of Haydn’s Andante in F minor
presented on his own, very good.
June 9: An attempt made in the lesson of the voice-leading line of Mendelssohn’s “Spring Song.”
June 15: On neighbor-note motion, precise graphs, in particular, examples from the Polonaise in C minor.
June 20: On the variation theme from Mozart’s Sonata in D major (cf. Albersheim).

I. 1927 (schriftlich): Urlinie zu Scarlatti Cdur 32; Volksausgabe; korrigiert im Januar 27.Diary January 3, 1927: “From Cube (letter): Urlinie of Scarlatti's C major [Sonata], No. 32 of the Volksausgabe[Leipzig: Breitkopf & Härtel, c. 1882]”; January 14: “10:30 with Brahms–Scarlatti, completed for the second time, finally to Cube's Urlinie.”; January 16: – “To Cube (letter): correction of his Urlinie.”; January 26: “From Cube (letter): he thanks me for the corrections, is already teaching at the Conservatory in Duisburg.”; – January 31: “To Cube (postcard): greetings; do not omit the linear progressions, however the solution may turn out.”
January 1927 (in writing): Urlinie for Scarlatti’s Sonata in C major, No. 32 of the Volksausgabe; corrected in January 1927.

tei:div.tei:note: The lesson reports for Angi Elias in the original are written continuously, without paragraph breaks or separating punctuation. They have been separated here in the interests of legibility.
tei:div.tei:ab: 4. X. Brahms op. 119 No 1, Linie begonnen
7. Jöde; Invention Bdur,>Fritz Jöde, Die Kunst Bachs, dargestellt an seinen Inventionen (Wolfenbüttel: Kallmeyer, 1926), the first chapter of which is devoted to the B major Invention. Bild.

9. Studien zum Genauesten hin angesetzt: Wieder-
-holung der Berçeuse u. Walzer Asdur.
14. Das Bild einer anderen Invention korrigiert.
16. Betrachtung der Themen in der Hohen Messe.
19. Brahms Bild zuende, Fingersatz u. Vortrag.
23. Bemerkungen zur Hohen Messe beendet.
26. Erläuterungen zum Buxbaum-Abend vom 25.: Beethoven op. 97 u. Schubert Dmoll.

28. Zum Vortrag der Hohen Messe, nach dem Konzert der Berliner Singakademie unter Schumann.Diary October 27: “In the evening, Mass in B minor, performed by the Berlin Choral Society under Schumann. A carefully nuanced performance, the chorus performing to its limits, in particular the sopranos in best voice. The extent to which this type of performance can be traced back to Schumann's predecessors, perhaps even as far back as Zelter, is not known to me; in any event most of the choral movements were worthy of praise, at most one could have wanted a more differentiated working through in the Kyrie. On the other hand, the arias disappointed, as always, lacking in all care: they lacked a precise agreement between the obbligato wind or string instrument and the voices, the clarification of the form and the modulations, and much else.”
30. Bild der Chopin-Etude op. 25 No 11, Am.
4. XI. Eine Aufgabe aus „Wie bist du, meine Königin“; über das Steckel-Quartett u. das eingesandte Hindemith-Quartett.

11. Korrektur des Bildes vom Thema der Eroica-Variationen op. 35; in die Wiederholung aufgenommen: Walzer Cism, Mazurka Asdur u. Gm.Diary November 11: “Work on the B-minor Etude, Op. 25, No. 10 (for Miss Elias).”

16. Linie zu Chopin Hm-Etude
op. 25 No 10, von mir vorher angegeben.

18. Ueber die Matthäus-Passion in Furtwänglers Aufführung.Performance in the Great Hall of the Musikverein Building, November 17, Gesellschaft der Musikfreunde regular concert, under Wilhelm Furtwängler, St Matthew Passion. — Diary November 9: “Miss Elias brings tickets to the final rehearsal of the St. Matthew Passion (8 shillings).”
20. Haydn Fantasie Cdur gelesen.
23. Fingersatz zur Hm-Etude.

2. XII. Zum Forellen-Quintett; über Meirecker u. van Berg,Diary November 29: “Buxbaum Quartet (with Meirecker), program: Schubert, Op. 161 in G major, the "Trout" Quintet, and the Quartet Movement in C minor (posthumous). [...] We look for Miss Elias in the gallery; I cancel tomorrow's lesson so that I can look at the collection.” über die Henrici-Sammlung.
4. Blick in das Capriccio von Haydn.
14. Etude Hm zuende.

16. Die fragliche Stelle aus Beethovens IV. Sinfonie (s. Albersheim).Cf. Albersheim lesson for November 29: “concerning a passage in Beethoven’s Fourth Symphony, first movement: B-sharp–C-sharp or B-natural–C-sharp.” Schenker is referring to the lower neighbor-note figure in the first violins at bar 290, towards the end of the development. The autograph score reads: d2–c2–b1–c2. So does Simrock’s 1823 edition of the score. But the old Gesamtausgabe and the Eulenburg score (edited by Max Unger) both give b1. Modern editions of the symphony, however, restore the autograph reading.

21. Ueber das Philharmonischen Konzert mit Weingartners op. 106, Egmont Ouvertüre u. die V. Sinfonie.Weingarten had made an orchestration of Beethoven’s String Quartet, Op. 106. – Schenker’s diary entry for December 19 has a lengthy description of this concert, which begins: “In the Philharmonic concert: Egmont Overture: all upbeats comprising three eighth-notes not played as upbeats – without striving towards a goal tone. As a result, the overture lost all its life, all its fire. Opus 106: in itself an inexcusable error, which demonstrates that Weingartner is not aware of the difference between a piano and orchestra, nor of the difference between writing for piano and for orchestra. [...]” — Diary December 19: “Work on Chopin's last Etude (for Miss Elias).”

23. Partitur zu op. 106 angesehen.This probably refers to the score of Beethoven’s “Hammerklavier” Sonata Op. 106 in Felix Weingartner’s orchestration: cf. lessonbook entry of December 21 and footnote.
28. Bild zur Etude Cm op. 25 No 12, treffend.

4. I. Etude Cm gespielt; Arie der Königin der Nacht aus der Zauberflöte gezeigt (s. Albersheim).Cf. Albersheim’s lesson for January 3: “The Queen of the Night’s aria from The Magic Flute: the coloratura completely underpinned by the voice-leading.”
8. Berçeuse wiederholt.
15. Haydn Capriccio.

18. Bemerkungen zum Furtwängler Konzert;Concert on January 15 in the Great Hall of the Musikverein, Vienna Philharmonic under Wilhem Furtwängler, program: Mendelssohn Symphony No. 3 (“Scottish”) and Brahms Symphony No. 2 in D major. — Diary January 28: “Elias has influenza.” Paganini-Variationen neu.
10. II. Bild des Basses in Haydns Capriccio.
15. Stücke aus dem Repertoire in Frau Pairamalls Gramophon angehört.
17. Ueber Gräser u. die Neuausgabe; Bilder zu den Paganini-Variationen.
26. Nocturne Esd op. 9 wiederholt.
1. III. Ueber das Konzert Bakhaus.
17. Aus Scarlatti-Brahms Heft 6 gezeigt.
5. IV. Klein‘s Metamorphosen vorgespielt.Diary April 5: “From Heinrich Fritz Klein, Linz, Metamorphoses on themes by Beethoven.”
7. Bilder zu den Paganini Variationen abgeschlossen.
14. Unerledigte Aufgaben aus früherer Zeit in Bildern; Brahms Gm-Quartett, Modulation im 1. Satz usw.

21. Aus der Hohen Messe: Einleitung zur Ddur-Arie im Bild;Probably the soprano duet “Christe eleison,” for which there are sketches and a fair copy of a graph in Elias’s hand (OC 81/4). einige Schubert-Walzer.
26. Aus Halm’s Buch;August Halm, Beethoven (Berlin: Max Hesse, 1927), which Schenker had just received from the publisher. Nachträge zur Nocturne Esd.

28. Bild
zum Cism-Walzer korrigiert; Korrekturen zur Appassionata (nach der von ihr geschenkten Handschrift) gezeigt.Diary April 28: “Miss Elias presents me with the original edition of Haydn, in twelve volumes.” — Diary March 10: “Miss Elias brings the facsimile edition of the "Appassionata," which she chanced to see in the window of the Perles bookshop.” Cf. Diary April 23–25: “Now I begin the correction of the "Appassionata" against the autograph facsimile.” – “Correction of the "Appassionata" completed.” – “To UE, the corrections to Op. 57 sent off.”
3. V. Paganini-Variationen als Ganzes wiederholt.
10. Vierhändig die Sinfonie von Haydn aus Bd III, s. Vrieslander.
12. Impromptu Fisd, neu, Bilder.
26. Fingersatz.Diary May 26: “In spite of the holiday, I will be teaching on June May 30: Brünauer, Elias, Pairamall.” – May 30,1927 was the Monday following Ascension Day.
28. Haydn Sonate Gd gelesen, Peters I, No 10 damit verglichen.
31. Vortrag des Impromptus.
7. VI. Vortrag des Impromptus ganz.
8. Schumann: vierhändige Original-Kompositionen.Diary June 8: “Three make-up lessons given (Elias, Hoboken).”
9. Brahms „Auf dem Kirchhof“, Bild korrigiert.Diary June 10: “Urlinie for Mendelssohn's "Spring Song" (for Brünauer) and for Chopin's Prelude in D major (for Elias).”
11. Wiederholt: Prélude Desd, Hm.
18. Bild zum Prélude Desd.
22. Vierhändig Streichquartett von Haydn Cd, op. 74; Brahms 1. Sinfonie, 1. u. 3. Satz.

tei:div.tei:note: The lesson reports for Angi Elias in the original are written continuously, without paragraph breaks or separating punctuation. They have been separated here in the interests of legibility.
tei:div.tei:ab: October 4: Brahms Op. 119, No. 1, voice-leading line begun.
October 7: Jöde; Invention in B major, graph.

October 9: Studies in the most precise way initiated:
revisiting of the Berceuse and the Waltz in A major.
October 14: The graph of a different invention corrected.
October 16: Consideration of the themes in the Mass in B minor.
October 23: Observations on the Mass in B minor finished.
October 26: Elucidations concerning the Buxbaum evening of the 25th: Beethoven Op. 97 and Schubert D minor.
October 28: On the performance of the Mass in B minor, after the concert given by the Berlin Choral Society directed by Schumann.
October 30: Graph of Chopin’s Etude in A minor, Op. 25, No. 11.
November 4: An assignment from Brahms’s song “Wie bist du, meine Königin”; concerning the Steckel Quartet and the quartet by Hindemith which was sent to me.
November 11: Correction of the graph of the theme of the “Eroica” Variations, Op. 35; taken up in repetition: Waltz in C minor, Mazurkas in A major and G minor.

November 16: Voice-leading line of Chopin’s Etude in B minor,
Op. 25, No. 10, previously indicated by me.
November 18: On the St. Matthew Passion, in Furtwängler’s performance.
November 20: Haydn’s Fantasy in C major read.
November 23: Fingering for the Etude in B minor.
December 2: On the “Trout” Quintet; concerning Meirecker and van den Berg, concerning the Henrici collection.
December 4: Glimpse of Haydn’s Capriccio.
December 14: Etude in B minor finished.
December 16: Die questionable passage from Beethoven’s Fourth Symphony (cf. Albersheim).
December 21: Concerning the Philharmonic concert with Weingartner’s Op. 106, “Egmont” Overture, and Fifth Symphony.
December 23: The score of Op. 106 examined.
December 28: Graph of the Etude in C minor, Op. 25, No. 12, to the point.
January 4: Etude in C minor played; I show her the Queen of the Night’s aria from The Magic Flute (cf. Albersheim).
January 8: Berceuse revisited.
January 15: Haydn’s Capriccio.
February 10: Graph of the bass line in Haydn’s Capriccio.
February 15: Pieces from Mrs. Pairamall’s phonograph record library listened to.
February 17: Concerning Graeser and his new edition; graphs for the Paganini Variations.
February 26: The Nocturne in E major from Op. 9 revisited.
March 1: On the Backhaus concert.
March 17: I show her things from Scarlatti–Brahms, volume 6.
April 5: I play to her Klein’s Metamorphosen.
April 7: Graphs for the Paganini Variations completed.
April 14: Unfinished assignments from an earlier time, in graphs; Brahms Quartet in G minor, modulation in the first movement, etc.
April 21: From the Mass in B minor: the introduction to the Aria in D major, graphed; some Schubert waltzes.
April 26: From Halm’s book; additional remarks on the Nocturne in E major.

April 28: Graph
of the C minor Waltz corrected; I show her corrections to the “Appassionata” (according to the facsimile edition of the manuscript she gave me).
May 3: Paganini Variations revisited, as an entire work.
May 10: The Haydn symphony from vol. III played four-hands, cf. Vrieslander.
May 12: Impromptu in F major, new; graphs.
May 26: Fingering.
May 28: Haydn’s Sonata in G major read; Peters edition, vol. I, No. 10, compared with it.
May 31: Performance of the Impromptu.
June 7: Performance of the Impromptu complete.
June 8: Schumann: original compositions for piano duet.
June 9: Brahms’s “Auf dem Kirchhof”, graph corrected.
June 11: Revisited: the preludes in D major and B minor.
June 18: Graph of the Prelude in D major.
June 22: Played four-hands: Haydn String Quartet in C major, Op. 74, and Brahms First Symphony, first and third movements.

tei:div.tei:ab:
1. X. Dreist. Satz, 5. Gattung; Jakob
Fischers Aufsatz.Jacob Fischer, Erläuterungen zur Interpunktionsausgabe (Berlin-Lichterfelde: Schlesinger’sche Buch- & Musikhandlung, 1926). See OC 45/2 for a copy with markings.

5. Jöde Invention Bdur.Fritz Jöde, Die Kunst Bachs, dargestellt an seinen Inventionen (Wolfenbüttel: Kallmeyer, 1926). The first chapter is devoted to the Invention in B major: Der rhythmisch-dynamische Pendelschlag (Invention No. 14 B-dur), pp. 15–50. Diary Oct 15: “Hoboken said that ‘the way of viewing the Invention in B major shows the contrast between Jöde and myself: that interested me greatly. First, I would like to learn many pieces in order to gain the correct perspective; then I can indeed work in much greater detail – if I stick to it.’”

8. Fragen der Metrik nach Wiehmayer.Theodor Wiehmayer, Über die Grundfragen der musikalischen Rhythmik und Metrik, Sonderdruck aus dem Bericht über den Musikwissenschaftlichen Kongress zu Leipzig vom 4.–8. Juni 1925 (Leipzig: Breitkopf & Härtel, [1925]). See OC 45/4 for a copy with markings, and OC 45/5 for another work by Wiehmayer.

12. Metrik nach Marpurg, FischerJacob Fischer, Erläuterungen zur Interpunktionsausgabe (Berlin-Lichterfelde: Schlesinger’sche Buch- & Musikhandlung), 1926). See OC 45/2 for a copy with markings. in seinen Beispielen, dazu aus der Deklamation im Requiem von Brahms; Bemerkungen zum Rosé-Abend:Concert in the middle recital hall of the Vienna Konzerthaus: Rosé String Quartet: Beethoven Op. 18, No. 1, in F major; Op. 127 in E major; Op. 59, No. 2, in E minor. Beethoven Streichquartett op. 18 No 1 u. Esd op 127 u. op. 59 No 2.

15. Zu Beethovens op. 18 No 2 u. 59 No 1; Bach Sarabande nach meiner VorlageHeinrich Schenker, Joh. Seb. Bach: Suite III C-dur für Violoncello-Solo, Sarabande, Meisterwerk II (1926), 97–104 (Eng. transl., vol. II, pp. 55–58). zuende geführt. Zurück zur Metrik.

20. I.: In op. 111: Der Schlusstriller u. mein Fingersatz; Antwort: 15/35/35 u. 45/45, nicht trillermäßig 153/535, nicht 454/5; dann Brahms Streichquartett Cm, 2. Satz, Tonart Fm oder Cm? Antwort: Fm.Diary January 23: “To Weisse (postcard): I explain the misunderstanding regarding the fingering and the tonality question arising from I–III–V, for which the recapitulation offers the proof at the analogous point – thus Brahms is in the right, in spite of his (Weisse's) opinion.” — The postcard in question is not known to survive. — Schenker draws a five-line stave below to mark the end of the saison’s notes.

January 20: In Op. 111: the concluding trill, and my fingering; answer: 15/35/35 and 45/45, not in the manner of a trill 153/535, not 454/545. Then: Brahms’s String Quartet in C minor, second movement, is it in the key of F minor or C minor? Answer: F minor.
